newsitem.title: JAMAICA: CRICKET-FORMER WEST INDIES TEST PLAYER HOLT DEAD AT 73.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-FORMER WEST INDIES TEST PLAYER HOLT DEAD AT 73.

text.p: Former West Indies and Jamaica batsman John Kenneth Constantine Holt, who once scored 166 runs in an innings against England, has died at the age of 73.
"JK" had been suffering from cancer for the past three years. He died on Wednesday.

Holt, a stylish batsman, scored 1,066 runs in 17 test matches against England, Australia, Pakistan and India. His top score of 166 came when he opened in the second test against England in 1954 -- an innings acknowledged as one of the finest seen at Kensington Oval in Barbados.
"He was such a wonderful cricketer in every respect," his former Jamaica and West Indies colleague Allan Rae said.
"He played the game extremely well and attractively and he was a great help to younger players when he was officially the coach in Jamaica."

In a first-class career which ended in 1962, Holt scored 4,256 runs with nine centuries at an average of 42.32. He captained Jamaica in 1961 and was vice-captain in the West Indies touring side to India and Pakistan in 1958-59.
